observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x00573d77: MOV ESI,ECX moves the receiver into ESI, which then carries it for the whole body; every field access is [ESI + disp]. EDX is never read, ruling out __fastcall. 0x00573f16: RET 0x8 pops two stack words, ruling out cdecl. Ghidra's decompilation labels it __thiscall with the receiver as param_1 and the first stack word as param_2.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: No value is returned. EAX and EBP are used as scratch; the two exits differ in whether EBP is restored before the pops, and neither leaves a meaningful EAX that any caller could use.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00573ef9..0x00573f04 and 0x00573f12..0x00573f16 are the two exits, both ending in RET 0x8 with no value contract. Every sampled caller discards the result.
observed_original_abi.termination: two exits: the early epilogue at 0x00573f04 and the shared epilogue at 0x00573f16

control_flow.early_exits: eight distinct early-exit edges, all to 0x00573f13 or to the fallthrough at 0x00573f12, which is the entry of the shared epilogue
control_flow.branch_polarity: The polarity is uniform and deliberate: nearly every guard is a JZ that SKIPS work rather than a JNZ that performs it. The two exceptions are the two flag-raising tests at 0x00573d7b / 0x00573d83 and 0x00573dc6, which skip the RAISE when the flag is already set, and the bit-11 test at 0x00573dfb, which skips the CLEAR when the bit is clear. The type test at 0x00573ec3 is JNZ, so a NON-match takes the shared epilogue and only a match continues. Reading the type test as JZ would invert the whole sibling-select tail.
control_flow.note_on_two_pushes: 0x00573e06 PUSH EBP and the matching POP at either 0x00573ef9 or 0x00573f12 keep the stack balanced across the four virtual calls in the outgoing and tail regions, each of which pops its own arguments. This is why the frame works without an EBP-based prologue.

semantic_contract: Invariants, in body order. (1) If part is null and flag editor+0x140 is zero, set +0x140 to 1. (2) If part equals the current primary at editor+0xe4, the function is a no-op unless the current primary is non-null AND its dword at +0x1c is non-zero; in that case it continues. (3) If the secondary at editor+0xf4 is non-null and differs from part, raise +0x140 to 1 if it is zero, and clear +0xf4. (4) If editor+0xe4 already equals part, stop. (5) If part is non-null and its dword at +0x10 is non-null and bit 11 of that object's dword at +0xdc8 is set, clear +0x140. (6) If the outgoing primary is non-null, drive its vtable slot +0x30 with (3,1); then, if flag editor+0x141 is non-zero, query its vtable slot +0x0c for type 0x50a993c and, when that yields a non-null object whose +0x10 is non-null, mark the matching list entry unselected with flag 1; then clear +0x141 unconditionally. (7) If part differs from the outgoing primary, AddRef part through its vtable slot +0x00, store it at editor+0xe4, then Release the outgoing primary through its vtable slot +0x04. (8) If editor+0xe4 is now null, call the audio port with (editor, 0). (9) Otherwise open the 0xd2cfe2ad marker, call 0x00573c00 with (0, -1), drive slot +0x30 with (0,1) on the newly published part, and read slot +0x10; if that equals 0x50a993c and +0x140 is non-zero, resolve the sibling of type 0x50a993c, mark the list entry holding it selected, set +0x141 to 1 and return through the early epilogue. The function writes no receiver byte other than +0x140, +0x141, +0xf4 and +0xe4. Its second stack argument is pushed by every observed caller and never read, so the reconstructed contract is insensitive to it. Net observable effect: the editor's primary part is replaced, the outgoing part is detached and the incoming one attached through the same two-argument virtual state slot with opposite first arguments, and a type-0x50a993c part additionally gets its sibling list entry kept in sync through a select/unselect handshake driven by the +0x141 flag.
classification_rationale: The complete 148-instruction body was read directly: the register-only frame shape, both stack arguments and the proof that the second is never read, all five receiver field accesses, the six virtual slot offsets with their argument lists, the two magic constants, the x87-free but EBP-balanced call sequence, all twenty-four basic blocks and every one of the twenty-two branch polarities. The receiver identity as the cEditor is proven from three SDK-named callers that use the same offsets, not merely inferred. Four material elements stay bounded and each is named. First, the concrete class behind the part's vtable: six slot offsets were disassembled but no table address was resolved, so no interface is named. Second, the meaning of the two flag bytes at +0x140 and +0x141: their complete read/write sets are established but nothing names them. Third, the meaning of the type id 0x50a993c, which is used consistently as both a query key and a comparison value but matches no SDK enumerator or TYPE constant. Fourth, the roles of 0x0043c3d0, 0x0043e760 and 0x0043e7e0, whose bodies establish a list index, a mark-selected and a mark-unselected respectively, but whose owning list type is unnamed. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for those four bounds and not for the body, which is complete; STRUCTURAL_ONLY would understate the evidence, since the state machine and the publish protocol are established rather than merely the layout.
semantic_findings: The function is a primary-part state machine, not a simple setter. Its whole body is a guard cascade that decides whether a publish is needed, and if so whether the type-0x50a993c sibling handshake must run.

A null part with an already-null primary is a complete no-op that reaches no port at all: 0x00573d98 CMP passes with both null, then 0x00573d9e JZ exits. The audio port at 0x00573f0a is reachable only when a non-null primary is being REPLACED by null.

The second stack argument is never read. The three SDK-named callers push 0x1, a register (EBP) and 0x1 respectively, and no instruction in the 148-instruction body touches the second word. The reconstruction declares it and marks it unused rather than inventing a meaning.

The publish order is addref-new, store, release-old: slot +0x00 on the incoming part at 0x00573e78, the store at 0x00573e7a, then slot +0x04 on the outgoing part at 0x00573e88. That ordering is what makes the swap safe against a re-entrant observer, and it is observable in the instruction order rather than inferred.

The +0xf4 secondary pointer is cleared with no refcount call, unlike the +0xe4 primary which is AddRef'd and Released. That asymmetry is a direct reading of the body and is worth flagging to any integrator who assumes both are refcounted.

The detach/attach pair is expressed through a single two-argument virtual slot: +0x30 with (3,1) on the outgoing part and (0,1) on the incoming one. Same slot, same second argument, opposite first argument, which reads as a state enum with 0 and 3 as the two endpoints.

The +0x141 flag is a one-shot handshake. It is set only at the very end of the 0x50a993c branch and consumed by the outgoing block of a LATER call, where it triggers the sibling unselect and is then cleared unconditionally -- including on the three early exits inside that block. The unconditional clear at 0x00573e61 is what prevents a failed unselect from being retried forever.

The type test at 0x00573ebe is necessary but not sufficient: 0x00573ecc additionally requires +0x140 to be set. So the sibling-select branch is reachable only when the flag has not been cleared, and 0x00573dfd is the instruction that clears it.

Bit 11 of the incoming part's +0xdc8 field is the same bit 0x00438700 reads on its own receiver, but the two uses are complementary: 0x00438700 uses it to GATE a call, this function uses it to CLEAR a flag. Two readers of one bit on opposite sides of a selection change is what makes the two functions part of one protocol.

0x00435ed0 and 0x00572020 are structurally the same four-slot marker helper, differing only in their leading tag id (0xd2cfe2ad versus the audio one) and their string ids. Both resolve their service through the single-instruction global accessor 0x00a206f0 returning DAT_0166d9f4. The audio port is therefore a sibling of the profiling marker, not an unrelated system call.

0x00572770 is a three-statement wrapper over exactly the inline query at 0x00573e2f -- same vtable offset +0x0c, same type id 0x50a993c -- which is a direct internal-consistency check on the 0x50a993c reading.
unresolved_questions: What class implements the part's vtable? Six slot offsets were disassembled (+0x00, +0x04, +0x0c, +0x10, +0x30 and the two marker-service slots) but no table address was resolved, so the interface is unnamed.

What is the type id 0x50a993c? It is used consistently as a query key at 0x00573e2a and as a comparison value at 0x00573ebe, and 0x00572770 corroborates the same pair, but no SDK enumerator and no SDK TYPE constant matches it. No name is asserted.

What do the flag bytes at +0x140 and +0x141 mean? Their complete read/write sets are established -- +0x140 is raised in three places, cleared in one and tested in one; +0x141 is set once, cleared once and tested once -- but nothing names either.
What is the dword at part+0x1c, whose non-zero value is the only thing that lets a re-selection of the same part proceed past the guard at 0x00573dab?
What is editor+0xf4, and is it really unrefcounted? The body clears it with no Release call, which is either intentional or a latent leak; static evidence cannot distinguish those.
What is the role of 0x00435ed0? Its four-slot marker shape with ascending tag ids suggests a scope or checkpoint, but no SDK name covers it and the role is not established.

Is 0x00572020 really Audio::StopAudio? The SDK lists its address and the argument shape matches, but the first argument passed here is the cEditor pointer rather than an AudioTrack and the callee tail-jumps into a service vtable.

Why do callers 0x00587480 and 0x00587cef duplicate two of this function's own guards immediately before calling it? Either the guards are load-bearing for a caller-side invariant or the compiler failed to see through them; not resolved.
Six of the ten reported call sites were not disassembled window-by-window in this batch; their receiver provenances come from the briefing's call graph.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists. Every flag value, every attribute bit, every list index and both 0x50a993c comparisons in the contract above are static readings of the code path, not observations.

A differential fixture would need to drive the editor through at least four transitions -- null-to-part, part-to-part, part-to-null and a 0x50a993c part swap -- and record whether the +0x141 handshake fires and in what order.
The original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run, so no stage-level reachability claim is made for this Editor-subsystem function.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 148-instruction body is reconstructed in full as machine-observable semantics, including the same-object guard, the secondary clear, the attribute-bit-11 flag clear, the outgoing detach/sibling-unselect block, the addref-store-release publish, both tails and the 0x50a993c handshake. All nine callees are declared as opaque ports and given no fabricated bodies.
preserved_semantics: the null-part flag raise happens before the same-object guard
the same-object guard requires BOTH a non-null primary and a non-zero part+0x1c, and exits on either failure
the secondary at +0xf4 is cleared without any refcount call, unlike the primary
the attribute-bit-11 test CLEARS +0x140 rather than gating a call
the outgoing block runs before the publish, and the +0x141 clear at 0x00573e61 is unconditional relative to the query outcome
the publish order is AddRef new, store, Release old
the audio port is taken only when +0xe4 is null AFTER the publish, i.e. only on a part-to-null transition
the 0x50a993c branch additionally requires +0x140 to be set, and ends by setting +0x141 and returning early
the second stack argument is declared and explicitly unused
the epilogue is callee-cleaned for both stack words (RET 0x8), modelled with __attribute__((thiscall))
not_reproduced: the register-only frame: the reconstruction uses ordinary C++ control flow and lets the compiler allocate stack, and drops the asymmetric late PUSH EBP / POP EBP that exists only to keep the four virtual calls' arguments balanced
the redundant reload of editor+0xe4 at 0x00573ee0 and the reload of `part` at 0x00573e5d, which are register-allocation artefacts rather than logic
the 425-byte length and the specific opcode encodings
body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: not claimed. The reconstruction is a plain C++ expression tree over declared ports; the original is 425 bytes in 148 instructions with a hand-managed register frame and six inline virtual dispatches.

validation.model_test_coverage: seven scenarios against a recording port trace: the null-part raise; arg2 insensitivity across 1 and 0xdeadbeef; the full publish path with slot +0x10 reporting 0x50a993c, asserting the publish, the +0x141 set, the +0x140 retention, the AddRef, the 0x00573c00 (0,-1) call, the (0,1) state call, the 0x50a993c query and the mark-selected with index 3, and the ABSENCE of the audio port; the null==null no-op, asserting that no port is reached at all; the part-to-null transition, asserting the Release and the audio port; the live-outgoing-part case with +0x141 set, asserting the (3,1) state call, the query, the Release and the +0x141 clear when slot +0x10 does not report 0x50a993c; and the secondary-clear case, asserting the +0xf4 clear and the +0x140 raise.
